summary: This sermon from James 1:1-4 teaches that followers of Jesus should pre-decide to view trials with joy, not as a natural emotional response but as a deliberate choice, because any type of trial—whether self-inflicted, caused by others, or due to living in a fallen world—can be used by God to produce spiritual maturity and conform believers to the image of Christ.
key_points: Pre-decide to have joy in trials because a positive outcome is possible
Various types of trials (self-inflicted, caused by others, effects of fallen world) can all lead to spiritual maturity
Trials are a 'cheat code' for spiritual growth—they conform us to Christ's image faster than good times
Spiritual maturity means becoming more like Jesus and lacking nothing, enabling us to help others in their trials
Jesus is our example and great high priest who suffered in every way yet chose not to sin
big_idea: The positive outcome of various trials is spiritual maturity, which happens when believers pre-decide to view difficulty with joy because they know God can use any trial to conform them to the image of Jesus.
title: Trial Positive
